approvalRequirements: Be a San Isabel Electric Association member with the charging equipment installed at an eligible member service address.
Be enrolled, or enroll, in the cooperative's current Off-Peak Plus charging program.
Purchase and install a new qualifying Level 2 charger and satisfy the applicable equipment and electrical-installation tier requirements.
Submit the current rebate claim with paid invoices or receipts, product information, installation documentation, and income documentation when claiming an income-qualified tier.
Comply with current quantity, timing, account-standing, and verification requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative currently publishes tiered Level 2 charger rebates under objective member, charging-program, equipment, installation, and documentation rules. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved after routine verification, subject to current program limits and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: San Isabel currently offers Level 2 charger rebates to qualifying members participating in Off-Peak Plus, with rebate tiers based on income and installation complexity and payment following claim review.

approvalRequirements: Be a San Isabel Electric Association member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a product or measure currently listed by the cooperative and meet its efficiency, sizing, equipment, and installation specifications.
Submit the rebate request within the current filing period, generally within 90 days of purchase or installation where stated.
Provide a paid itemized invoice or receipt, model and certification information, and contractor or installation documentation required for the selected measure.
Comply with applicable annual quantity limits and permit inspection or other verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: San Isabel's current residential rebates use published measure-specific rules and administrative documentation review rather than competitive selection. A timely, documented, qualifying claim is likely to be paid, subject to program limits and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Current San Isabel pages require member eligibility, a qualifying installed measure, timely submission, paid receipts or invoices, and product-specific documentation before a residential rebate is approved.

approvalRequirements: Be a San Miguel Power Association member with the measure installed at the eligible member account location.
Select a measure currently offered by the association and meet its equipment, efficiency, installation, and customer-class specifications.
Submit the online rebate application within 60 days of purchase or installation and by the applicable program-year deadline.
Provide itemized invoices or receipts, model and specification information, and any measure-specific contractor or installation records.
Permit inspection or verification, including inspection of claims above the published threshold and other projects selected for review, and apply while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: San Miguel publishes current prescriptive rebates with objective member, measure, timing, documentation, and inspection requirements. A conforming claim is likely to be approved while program funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: San Miguel's current rebate process requires installation at a member account, an online claim generally within 60 days, itemized documentation, and inspection for larger or selected projects while funds last.

approvalRequirements: Be a San Miguel Power Association member proposing an eligible renewable-energy system at a member service location.
Use an eligible solar photovoltaic or other currently supported renewable technology and satisfy the association's technical, safety, metering, and interconnection rules.
Submit the preliminary net-metering or distributed-generation application and receive permission to install before beginning construction.
Have the contractor submit the applicable rebate documentation and provide system design, equipment, invoice, permit, and as-built records.
Pass final inspection and interconnection review, execute the required agreements, and receive permission to operate before final incentive approval.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The renewable rebate follows a defined pre-installation interconnection and post-installation verification process rather than competitive scoring. An eligible project that receives advance approval and passes final review is likely to receive the published incentive, subject to current funds and limits.
reviews.evidenceText: San Miguel requires renewable projects to obtain preliminary interconnection approval before installation, submit contractor and system records, and pass final inspection and permission-to-operate review before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be the current eligible account holder for a Sangre de Cristo Electric Association service location and keep the account in good standing.
Purchase and install equipment or a measure currently eligible for an association energy-efficiency credit within the service territory.
Meet the applicable product, efficiency, contractor, installation, and operating requirements for the selected measure.
Submit the completed credit request with receipt or invoice, model and specification information, and other required records within 90 days where the current program states that deadline.
Permit inspection or other installation verification when required before the credit is applied.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The association's current credits use objective account, equipment, installation, timing, documentation, and inspection criteria. A complete qualifying request is likely to be approved after administrative verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Sangre de Cristo's current credit pages require an eligible account-holder purchase, service-area installation, timely documentation, and inspection before approval for measures that carry verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Santee Cooper commercial customer at the project location.
Select equipment or a project currently covered by EmpowerBusiness and meet the applicable technical, efficiency, installation, and customer requirements.

Obtain preapproval, a pre-installation inspection, or custom-project authorization before purchase or construction when the selected measure requires it, including qualifying lighting and nonprescriptive projects.
Submit the applicable calculator, workbook, application, equipment schedule, project-cost information, and supporting technical documentation.
Complete the approved work within the authorization period and provide final invoices, installation records, and access for post-installation inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: EmpowerBusiness is an active administrative incentive program with prescriptive and custom pathways rather than a competitively ranked grant. A project that obtains any required advance approval and passes final verification is likely to be paid, subject to program funds and caps.
reviews.evidenceText: Santee Cooper currently offers EmpowerBusiness incentives and requires advance approval or inspection for specified measures, followed by installation records, invoices, and final verification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Santee Cooper residential customer financing a currently eligible renewable-energy project.
Submit the loan and credit application and satisfy the lender's account, income, credit, repayment, and documentation requirements.
Provide the project proposal, contractor information, equipment details, and cost documentation required for the selected renewable measure.
Complete any required distributed-generation or interconnection application and receive project approval before installation.
Use a participating Trade Ally or other approved contractor where required and execute the loan documents within the approval period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The loan pathway is active but financing depends on borrower-specific credit underwriting, project eligibility, documentation, interconnection review, and loan terms. Eligibility for a renewable project does not by itself guarantee financing.
reviews.evidenceText: Santee Cooper's current home-energy loan process requires customer and credit approval before work, an eligible project, supporting contractor and cost records, and interconnection documentation for renewable generation.

approvalRequirements: Be an active Santee Cooper residential customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install equipment currently eligible under EmpowerHome and meet the measure's efficiency, sizing, product, and installation specifications.
Use a participating Trade Ally, appropriately licensed contractor, or other required installation pathway for the selected measure.
Submit the current application or contractor form with paid invoices or receipts, equipment ratings, model information, photographs, and other measure-specific records.
Allow Santee Cooper to verify the account, equipment, and completed installation before issuing the rebate.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: EmpowerHome publishes measure-specific residential rebates with objective customer, equipment, contractor, documentation, and verification rules. A complete qualifying installation is likely to receive the published rebate after review, subject to program limits and funding.
reviews.evidenceText: Current EmpowerHome pages require a qualifying installation and measure-specific application, contractor, efficiency-rating, purchase, and verification documents before a rebate is approved.

approvalRequirements: Be an active Santee Cooper customer proposing rooftop solar at an eligible service address.
Submit the distributed-generation or interconnection application, fee, design, and equipment information and receive approval before installation.
Use a participating Solar Trade Ally and install equipment that meets the program's safety, technical, metering, and certification requirements.
Submit the rebate application, contractor and equipment records, invoices, permits, and other required completion documents.
Pass final inspection and system acceptance, complete the meter exchange or other interconnection steps, and receive permission to operate before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: EmpowerSolar uses a defined interconnection, Trade Ally, installation, and final-acceptance process rather than competitive selection. A qualifying project that secures advance approval and passes final review is likely to receive the rebate, subject to current funds and program limits.
reviews.evidenceText: Santee Cooper currently requires rooftop-solar customers to obtain interconnection approval, use an approved installation pathway, and complete final inspection, acceptance, and meter steps before the rebate is issued.

approvalRequirements: Be a Satilla REMC member proposing an eligible home energy improvement.
Submit the proposed project for Satilla REMC prescreening and satisfy the cooperative's account, property, measure, contractor, and project requirements.
Apply through Go Energy Financial Credit Union and provide the borrower, income, credit, project, and contractor documentation requested for underwriting.
Pass the credit union's credit and repayment review and accept the approved financing terms.
Use the approved contractor and execute the required loan and project documents before eligible work begins.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: HomePlus is a financing program rather than an automatic incentive. Approval depends on both cooperative project prescreening and separate credit-union underwriting, so an eligible improvement may receive financing but is not assured of it.
reviews.evidenceText: Satilla's HomePlus process is contingent on cooperative prescreening and separate Go Energy Financial Credit Union approval before work and financing can proceed.

approvalRequirements: Be an active Sawnee EMC commercial member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a measure currently eligible for the applicable program year and meet its equipment, efficiency, customer, and installation requirements.
Submit the current rebate request by the stated deadline with itemized paid invoices or receipts, product specifications, and required contractor or installation records.
Allow Sawnee EMC to verify the member account, project location, equipment, and completed installation, including an inspection when requested.
Apply while the annual rebate budget remains available and comply with program caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Sawnee's current commercial incentives are rules-based and use member, equipment, timing, documentation, and verification criteria rather than competitive scoring. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be approved while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Sawnee's current incentives require program-year qualifying work, itemized purchase records, and member-site verification, with approved amounts subject to annual program funds and limits.

approvalRequirements: Be an active Sawnee EMC residential member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a product or measure currently eligible for the program year and satisfy its efficiency, equipment, rate, and installation requirements.
Submit the online rebate claim by the current deadline with paid invoices or receipts, model and specification information, and any measure-specific records.
For an electric-vehicle charger claim, meet the current Level 2 charger, installation, account, and documentation conditions.
Permit visual, account, or site verification and apply while the annual rebate budget remains available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Sawnee currently offers prescriptive member incentives under objective measure, documentation, timing, and verification rules. A conforming residential claim is likely to be approved while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Sawnee's current residential offers require qualifying current-year purchases, complete supporting documentation, measure-specific conditions, and post-installation verification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Have submitted a Charge Ready application before Southern California Edison closed the application portal to new projects.

Meet the applicable site, customer, parking, charger-count, accessibility, and program-configuration requirements and execute the fully signed program agreement by the current deadline for existing projects.
Purchase only program-approved charging equipment and do not purchase or install equipment before receiving the required project approval.
Complete the approved make-ready infrastructure and charging-equipment installation and satisfy applicable rate, demand-response, networking, operation, maintenance, and data requirements.
Submit final invoices, permits, equipment, installation, and completion records and pass Southern California Edison inspection and verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Southern California Edison no longer accepts new Charge Ready applications. Only applicants already in the pipeline can continue through agreement, construction, documentation, and inspection, so a new opportunity record is unlikely to produce an award.
reviews.evidenceText: Southern California Edison states that Charge Ready applications are no longer accepted; existing approved projects must complete agreements, approved equipment procurement, installation, documentation, and final verification.

reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Southern California Edison's current multifamily page is a resource hub for separate programs and does not identify one active, standalone rebate process matching this legacy record or an incentive for benchmarking compliance alone. Current approval requirements and award likelihood cannot be established without selecting a specific successor offering.
reviews.evidenceText: The current multifamily page directs property owners to separate resources and programs but does not substantiate a single active rebate matching the legacy record or benchmarking compliance as an awardable measure.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Southern California Edison nonresidential customer with an account and project that meet current on-bill financing rules.

Confirm that the proposed battery-storage project qualifies through a current Southern California Edison incentive or financing pathway; the current on-bill financing page does not expressly list general standalone battery storage.
Submit the on-bill financing application, project matrix, customer and contractor records, and other documents required for credit and project evaluation.
Receive written financing and project approval before purchasing or installing the financed equipment.
Complete the approved work, submit the installation report and final invoices, and pass post-installation inspection before funds are released.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: On-bill financing remains subject to customer credit review, project eligibility, advance approval, and final inspection. The mapped standalone battery-storage scope is not expressly supported by the current eligible-category description, so project-specific confirmation is required.
reviews.evidenceText: Southern California Edison's current on-bill financing process requires credit and project approval before installation and final inspection afterward; current listed pathways do not clearly establish general standalone battery-storage eligibility.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Southern California Edison residential customer for the current successor offering selected.

Choose a currently available program that actually covers the proposed measure, such as a smart-thermostat enrollment incentive, an instant product rebate, or an eligible targeted home-performance offering.
Satisfy the selected program's customer, product, location, income, contractor, and installation requirements.
Complete any required enrollment, eligibility verification, pre-purchase coupon, assessment, or reservation step before purchase or installation.
Provide the requested purchase, equipment, installation, account, and verification records before payment or bill credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Southern California Edison currently offers separate residential pathways for thermostats and selected efficiency products, but the legacy aggregate rebate record no longer has one uniform approval process and does not establish that every mapped HVAC measure is currently covered.
reviews.evidenceText: Southern California Edison now routes residential incentives through separate programs, including smart-thermostat enrollment, instant product rebates, and targeted home-performance pathways with different eligibility and approval steps.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying San Diego Gas & Electric commercial customer in the service area and meet the current account, rate, and business-eligibility rules.
Select a measure currently supported by SD Energy Edge; current materials support specified HVAC and exterior-lighting measures but do not support indoor LED lighting.
Complete the applicable site survey, proposal, letter of authorization, and project documentation steps.
Obtain preapproval before purchase or installation for custom projects; for eligible already-installed prescriptive measures, submit the claim and invoices within 90 days.
Complete installation, submit final application and invoices, and pass the required post-installation inspection while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program is active for qualifying commercial customers and specified HVAC and exterior-lighting measures, but the generic LED mapping is only partially supported because current materials exclude indoor LED rebates. Approval also depends on the correct prescriptive or custom pathway and available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: SD Energy Edge currently supports specified commercial HVAC and exterior-lighting measures, requires custom-project preapproval, allows eligible prescriptive claims within 90 days, excludes indoor LED rebates, and conducts post-installation inspection.

approvalRequirements: Have been accepted into Power Your Drive Workplaces before San Diego Gas & Electric closed the program to new applications.
Own or control the eligible workplace site for the required participation period and satisfy the current site, parking, customer, and electrical-service conditions.
Own, operate, and maintain the charging equipment for the required period and use equipment meeting the program's technical and networking requirements.
Complete the approved load-management plan, easement or access arrangements where required, construction, permits, and installation.
Submit completion documentation and pass San Diego Gas & Electric inspection and verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: San Diego Gas & Electric states that Power Your Drive Workplaces is fully subscribed and is not accepting applications. Only previously accepted participants can complete the remaining site, construction, and verification steps.
reviews.evidenceText: Power Your Drive Workplaces is fully subscribed and closed to new applications; existing participants must satisfy site-control, charger ownership and maintenance, load-management, construction, and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible San Diego Gas & Electric residential customer under the current successor program selected.
Verify that the proposed product or home improvement is currently covered and meet the program's account, product, income, location, and installation requirements.
For an instant Golden State Rebate, complete eligibility verification and obtain the coupon before purchase and select a currently qualifying product.
For the Energy Savings Assistance pathway, submit the interest or application form, complete income and account verification, obtain owner approval where needed, and complete the home assessment.
Complete installation and any required inspection or documentation review before the incentive or no-cost improvement is finalized.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current thermostat, heat-pump water-heater, room-air-conditioner, and income-qualified home-improvement pathways exist, but the legacy broad residential-efficiency record no longer has one uniform approval process and does not substantiate every mapped HVAC measure.
reviews.evidenceText: San Diego Gas & Electric's current product rebates use eligibility verification and pre-purchase coupons, while its income-qualified home-improvement program uses account and income screening, a home assessment, installation, and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Seattle City Light commercial or industrial customer at the project location.
Select a currently supported measure and meet the applicable equipment, efficiency, operating, customer, and installation rules.
For a simple rebate, submit the required product and purchase documentation within 90 days where the current pathway permits post-purchase filing without preapproval.

For a custom, major retrofit, or performance-based project, submit the project application, technical scope, savings calculations, and cost information and receive any required authorization before installation.
Complete the project, provide final invoices and installation records, and pass inspection or savings verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Seattle City Light maintains active simple and custom commercial incentive pathways. These are administrative rather than competitively ranked, so a qualifying project using the correct pathway is likely to be paid after documentation and verification, subject to program limits and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Seattle City Light currently offers simple rebates that may be filed within 90 days and larger custom or performance pathways requiring project review, documentation, and final verification.

approvalRequirements: Construct an eligible multifamily project in Seattle City Light's service territory and design it to exceed the applicable energy code baseline.
Enroll in the current Energy Design Assistance pathway before design documents are complete and before the project is too advanced for program analysis.
Provide project plans, energy-model information, equipment and envelope selections, schedules, ownership information, and other design documentation.
Execute the Seattle City Light participation or funding agreement at least three months before the temporary certificate of occupancy or other stated project milestone.
Construct the approved design and provide as-built records, commissioning or testing information, and access for post-construction verification before final payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current new-construction pathway uses early design enrollment, a signed funding agreement, objective above-code performance, and final verification rather than competitive selection. A properly enrolled project that delivers the approved design is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Seattle City Light's current multifamily new-construction pathway requires early enrollment, a signed funding agreement before occupancy, an above-code design, and post-construction verification.

approvalRequirements: Own or rent an eligible home in Seattle, or meet the current Seattle City Light service-area and electric-heating conditions for an eligible property outside the city.
Meet the current household-income limits and other occupancy, property, and program eligibility rules.
Submit the HomeWise application with proof of identity, residence, household income, utility account, property ownership or tenancy, and other requested documentation.
Obtain property-owner consent and satisfy rental-property conditions when the applicant is a tenant or landlord.
Complete the program energy audit and accept the program-approved scope, contractor, installation, and inspection process.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: HomeWise uses defined location, income, documentation, and home-assessment rules and directly manages qualifying weatherization work. An eligible household that completes screening and the audit is likely to receive approved services, subject to program capacity and property feasibility.
reviews.evidenceText: HomeWise screens applicants for location and income, verifies household and property documents, conducts a home energy audit, and then selects and manages qualifying no-cost weatherization work.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible California utility customer or host site and select a currently eligible Self-Generation Incentive Program technology, customer category, budget, and territory.
Use an eligible registered applicant or developer and equipment that meets current program, safety, certification, warranty, interconnection, and performance requirements.
Confirm that the applicable budget category and utility territory are accepting reservation requests and have available funds at the current incentive step.
Submit the reservation request before installation with the required customer, site, technology, cost, developer, and eligibility documentation.
Meet project-milestone deadlines, complete installation and interconnection, submit the incentive claim, and pass field inspection and performance verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Self-Generation Incentive Program participation is rules-based, but awardability varies materially by technology, customer category, utility territory, incentive step, and remaining budget. A project must first secure a valid reservation and then satisfy milestones and final verification.
reviews.evidenceText: The 2026 program uses reservation, project-milestone, and incentive-claim forms with developer, equipment, interconnection, inspection, and performance requirements; current availability varies by category and utility territory.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible commercial or multifamily property with at least four units in the City of St. Louis; the current program is not available for ordinary residential properties.
Propose a permanent eligible energy-efficiency, renewable-energy, water, or resilience improvement and obtain project-specific confirmation that the proposed battery-storage system is eligible.
Provide an energy or savings analysis showing a savings-to-investment ratio greater than one and submit the signed contractor bid and project-cost information.
Be current on taxes, assessments, mortgages, and other property obligations, satisfy solvency and lien conditions, and obtain senior-lender consent.
Pass program review and private capital-provider underwriting, execute the assessment and financing documents, and close before construction begins.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Set the PACE St. Louis currently provides commercial financing, not an automatic rebate. Approval depends on property and project eligibility, positive savings economics, lender consent, private underwriting, and successful closing; battery-storage eligibility remains project-specific.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program is commercial-only and requires an eligible city property, positive savings analysis, senior-lender consent, owner and tax standing, program review, private underwriting, and financing close before work.

approvalRequirements: Be a Shakopee Public Utilities business customer at the project location.
Submit the proposed project through the current online commercial-rebate process with customer, measure, equipment, cost, and estimated energy-savings information.
Receive program eligibility review and an authorization number before purchasing equipment or beginning work when required.
Complete the authorized project within the same calendar year and no later than the current maximum completion period, generally 12 months.
Provide final invoices, equipment and installation records, and any requested verification documentation while program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Shakopee Public Utilities uses a defined administrative review and authorization process and states that funds are held for eligible authorized projects. A qualifying project is likely to receive the incentive after timely completion and documentation, subject to limited annual funds and program discretion.
reviews.evidenceText: Shakopee Public Utilities reviews online submissions before authorization, holds funds for eligible projects, requires timely completion and final records, and limits awards to available program funds.
